label: Option B executed: r1.jsonl diffed against all derived sets (render + content mix) — no training
findings: Render/provenance is CLEAN: training/tool-schemas.json byte-identical to src TOOL_SCHEMAS; the system prompt embedded in r1 pairs byte-identical to today's BEGINNER_SYSTEM_PROMPT (uniform across all 32); no message-ordering or role anomalies; nothing renders over 1536 tokens except 1-2 derivative rows (1589 max) — truncation can only ever have mattered to r6.
Tool mix: r1 = 32 write_file + 2 list_files, ZERO read_file/edit_file/run_command. Derivatives: read_file 34-52, edit_file 17-42, run_command 11.
Chain depth: r1 = 30/32 single tool call (avg 1.06). Derivatives avg 1.86-3.19 calls/row.
Writes: r1 = 21/32 multiline full-file content. Curated/r7 = 7/43 and 7/57 multiline (mostly single-line appends/snippets).
Style: r1 prompts avg 66 chars, summaries avg 136 chars, mixed */- bullets; curated/r7 prompts 151-163 chars, summaries ~296 chars, uniform - bullets.

Eval cross-ref (multi tier): r1 passes 8,9,10,12,13,16; derivatives consistently FAIL 12 (append to list — they append and lose existing lines) and 13 (JSON edit — edit_file old_text misses) and mostly 15 (read-transform-write precision); r5/r7 additionally fail 16 (exact one-line copy). These are precisely the modify-existing-content and exact-extraction tasks.

Irony: derivative edit_file demonstrations are themselves correct (short old_text/new_text), yet models trained on them fail edit-style tasks — while r1, never shown edit_file, solves edits by read -> write_file the FULL new content, which cannot lose untouched fields and passes strict verifiers.
conclusion: r1's score is carried by its narrow, redundant curriculum: short prompts, single whole-file write_file completions, precise full content. Derived sets teach edit_file/chain SHAPES the 7B imitates without the exact-match skill, breaking the very tasks they were meant to fix. Winning recipe = many small full-file writes, NOT one exemplar per shape.
next: Round 8 candidate: r1's 32 pairs + ~10-15 synth pairs in r1's own style that cover eval shapes via READ -> write_file(FULL content) (never edit_file), keeping 66-char-style prompts and 136-char summaries. Train r1 recipe (6ep/1536, ~2 min/step). If multi recovers without core loss, edit_file demonstrations are banned from training data.

verdict: Scaffold-v2.1 is the best pixie-7b configuration ever measured: median 57.5/72 (+5 over v2, +5 over frozen r1's band) with a record 62/72 single run, multi median at the 6/9 ceiling for the first time as a MEDIAN (v2 only touched it in single runs), and #15 passing for the first time in project history. No hard-tier regression and no round-cost increase. The remaining 0/12 tasks fail for reasons nudges cannot reach: wrong-premise tool outputs (#14), no write-through after narration (#23), and per-file multi-write persistence (#20).
